text_fidelity_a:
Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig [[VIDEOID:f267642283bcf2ef6b127013dc46be9b]] On the advertising, this says that it shoots 20 feet. I was really skeptical, and I was expecting it to only shoot 20 feet in the air. Now, I don't have a 20 foot ladder, so I can't tell for sure, but I'm pretty sure that this will shoot vertically 20 feet, and horizontally maybe even a little more.

The truck is big and bulky, which I really liked. And there are no small, removable parts, so it's probably good for kids of any age. It does shoot a pretty powerful stream of water, so the only danger is squirting friends, family, and pets in the eye.

Now, about the water, the truck doesn't hold very much water. It says that it will shoot 50 shots of water, and it does do that. This is a lot like one of those water conserving showers. It really doesn't use very much water, but you can't really tell that until you fill it up. So, it's not the best thing for a water fight. But it is a great gift for youngsters so they don't get their siblings too wet. And I did really like the bright, vivid colors.

The wheels rotate, but they can't turn. If you need to turn this, you'll need to pick it up and move it around. Really, the only movable part on this is the fire hose.

Pros:
+Big and bulky
+Fun for all ages
+Shoots water a long way
+You can position the fire hose a little

Cons:
-A little hard to aim
-Wheels can't turn right or left, only rotate straight ahead
-Doesn't hold a ton of water
-You can't build up pressure to do a power squirt
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig

BraveRats - A Game by Seiji Kanai After attempting to play this game, I was confused. Honestly, I went to look around at reviews to see what I was missing. I saw such words as “bluffing” and “strategy” and I was left with, “What?!” It seemed like I had a completely different game. It takes a little time to understand everything, though. Without the cheat sheet close by, it was impossible for me to figure out who won. Even then, the “special powers” confused me. The cheat sheet would tell me the winner of a certain combination, but then according to the “special powers”, the other card should have won. (After reading through the instructions again, I saw that the special powers always override the cheat sheet.) I’m embarrassed about my confusion, but I’m throwing it out there in case I can make anybody else out there that’s confused like me feel better.

There are 8 red cards, 8 blue cards, a cheat sheet, and a booklet, all in a tin case. It’s a very quick game. Though it seems like it would be simple, it can be complicated at first. Once you get the hang of it, it is simple, though.

I imagine this will be a perfect game to play with my little ones when they’re a bit older. (My oldest is a delayed 5 right now, but I imagine slightly older children will have fun with this!)

Really, once the initial confusion is dealt with, this is a fun little game!
text_fidelity_b: BraveRats - A Game by Seiji Kanai

Radio Flyer 6V Battery Powered Bumper Car, Electric Ride On with Remote, Toddler Ride On Toy for Ages 1.5+ Years Simply Excellent, you set the control amount, then place the young driver in.
Control amounts:
Parental - you have a remote control, and can drive your little speedster wherever you want to.
Youngster - your race car driver has full control over the vehicle
Mixed - should the little one be racing towards danger, you can override their controls and save the day.

The biggest problem with this is refraining from showing your young driver what it would atke to cause an airbag to deploy! (There are no airbags installed, and no children were hurt in the making of this review!)

The car is easy for young hands to control, and good fun! The remote is easy to operate. The car travels at the speed of a slow walk, yet the screams and giggles will make you think it is going a lot faster!

The battery lasts a long time, I didn't actually time a full charge to empty but noticed in all my (extensive) testing I had to recharge it only once.
Well made, easy to put together, a good 30 minutes though, so be prepared.

This will cause smiles and joy for a long time. Its really well thought out and built.

The kickstand is terrible. You either have to hold it or lay it flat to put the pegs in but even then it rocks side to side easily. When you use the kickstand a slight bump to the top of the unit could knock it over.

The bezel is also too wide and I also don't understand the reason for the extended parts of the black plastic on the side. With such a wide bezel you don't need them and it would like nicer as a square.

My unit does not glow evenly. I opened it to see if something wasn't working. Everything was but there just weren't enough lights, one more and a little adjustment would've helped. The unit is also on a timer. As it runs on batteries having it lit all the time would likely drain them. They should have added a USB port and just not included the cable. You're not able to keep it powered on 24/7. It's maybe a 10 minute timer. Pressing the button multiple times changes the light mode: lit, 3 section rotating flashing light show, full on off blink and the last one turns the 4 LEDs on 1 at a time and then off 1 at a time.

I made one of the provided examples and I had just enough pegs of a few colors. a few extras would been nice.

The sticker on mine was very crooked and out of place.

However, where the LEDs do light the unit right, it does look cool. I think, way better than the OG, they're more neon glow, the colors are much better, instead of a yellow glow the LEDs are bright white which allows you to have yellow, pink, orange, blue and white pegs. These colors on the dark background are nice.
The pegs stay in nicely. I've only made one picture but not one has fallen out. It may not hold up to repeated removing and placing of the pegs but I plan on leaving it with a certain design for a while.

This would be awesome if it just had a few improvements. I'd probably buy another

Hasbro, you can do better than this. For an MSRP of $19.99 it's not worth it. Even Amazon's marked down price is too high. This is something I'd expect to see at 5 and below.

It is on the weird side(even thought so from my 3 boys), with all the noises, but it is also on the humorous side. To play, you stick a bit of slime("food") into the bone. The players take turns rolling the die and squeezing the bone the amount rolled. Each player has a shovel that they place behind the dog to catch the "doos" before squeezing the bone. Each time the dog poos, you have to refill the bone. Once all the slime is gone, the player with the most "doos" wins. Had I known that the game used slime, I never would have gotten it. I've had to throw out too many items ruined from it to want it in my home anymore. We just try to be extra careful when playing. It comes with two bags, but it only takes one to play. The second bag is for if the first gets ruined. It says on the bag that it's non-toxic, but to still wash hands after touching it. When the game works, it's fun and makes us laugh. We've had lots of trouble getting it to work properly, though. Many times it won't seal just right(I guess) and no amount of squeezing the bone will make anything happen. It warns not to put too much, which we've tried not to do, and to also make sure the bone is pushed all the way in, which we've tried to do. It still won't work for us half the time, though, which makes it frustrating. If the slime ever gets stuck, the game does come with a stick to push it out. Children of all ages and even grown men cannot resist chucking it as far as they can. These big rings sail FAAAAR! And they are a tad prone to getting stuck in high and sometimes funny places. (Believe me, these will end up in the trees and on roofs but they are easy to get down with a broom stick because of their ring shape.)

A boy at cub scouts had one of these that everyone was playing with last week. My son decided to spend his hard earned allowance money on Amazon to order one, hoping it wouldn't be pink. :) He was thrilled when a yellow ring arrived. It has a VERY rice, silicone-like, soft rubbery grip and is fun to throw! Kids fight over these rings so I'm thinking of ordering several for birthday gifts and cousin Christmas gifts. You can't beat a gift for under ten that kids actually want to play outside with!

Consider spending a little more and buying the 13 inch ring. It flies farther and better than the 10 inch rings did. However, if you don't have a wide open play space, the 10 inch rings might be better because they play more like a Frisbee and don't get hung up in trees quite as easily.

UPDATE: I am now buying our THIRD ring! These make awesome gifts for boys in the 8 to 11 range, as my son is frequently swarmed by boys wanting to play with his. But be aware that if you throw it too far and loose sight of it, you won't get it back. It will be stolen by the first kid who comes across it. We had this happen at a party where the ring ended up sailing over a house and landing far behind it in an empty field right at dark. It was snatched before daylight. Hence me having to buy our third. (Since it was probably the roving neighborhood teenagers who picked it up late that night, I am going to say this is a good toy for fussy 16 and 17 year-olds, too!) It has been a favorite gift at birthday parties, followed by thank yous from the moms who are grateful for any toy that gets their video game addicted boys outside. I am thrilled to have found such a good gift for under $10. You can't go wrong with this ring!

Update March 2017: I have now ordered nearly 10 of these rings in the last 5 months for birthday gifts for 9 and 10 year old boys and without fail, it has been an instant hit. The boys are always eager to show how FAR they can throw the ring and then are shocked when it sails two hundred yards or more. They puff out their chests as their friends exclaim "WOOOAH!" while the ring whizzes one or two streets over and then the birthday boy swaggers off to fetch the ring with every other boy tagging along, begging for a turn to throw it next. Children now double check with my son to ensure that he's going to get them an Aerobie ring for their birthday. I keep at least one on-hand for last minute birthday party invites.

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Monopoly E Electronic Banking What can you possibly say new about Monopoly, the world's favorite property trading game, that hasn't already been said for decades since it's introduction by Parker Brothers in 1935? No matter what new version of Monopoly comes out, it's always so much fun to play with family and friends.

In the sixties, we always had one major problem when the entire family sat down to a long night of playing Monopoly, and that was, we always ran out of money if the game went on long enough. There used to be an office store named Burrows that sold extra Monopoly money and buying an extra packet or two was the only solution to our money shortage.

Now with this new version of Monopoly With Electronic Banking, you'll never run out of money, because there isn't any. The game comes with the standard board, dice, houses, hotels, Title Deed cards, Chance and Community Chest cards, 6 tokens and 6 bank cards that slide through an electronic banking unit which keeps track of your cash on your card. The electronic unit takes 2 AAA batteries (Not Included) and can store millions of dollars on each player's bank card.

It actually takes just as long to type in the money you accumulate on each player's card, as it does to hand count the cash to the players, so don't think this electronic unit is a time saver. We actually found when playing with 6 players, that it saved time to have a separate banker. This electronic banking version of Monopoly may not be faster than the cash version, but it's every bit as fun and that's saying a lot for a game that's been rated number one for over 75 years!
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Monopoly E Electronic Banking

iTikes Map This is such an amazing educational toy! My 4 year old is already learning new words. He's learning about different cultures and animals. He was thrilled that there is a solar system map included, since he is obsessed with all things concerning the solar system right now.

There are 6 maps included:
Solar System
Dinosaurs
World Cats
World Dogs
World Facts
World Music

There are a few things that could use improvement, though. If you don't keep the thing turned upright, the maps will fall out. The clear top won't latch very well. If your little ones happen to turn it upside down, you'll most likely be picking up maps. Also, there is a slight delay between touching the stylus on a picture and anything being said. My son got a little impatient sometimes. At times, I even wondered if it was working. There were also times that we touched the picture over and over before it would work.

Overall, while it can be annoying at times with not working right, I found it worth it due to the educational/fun value. Getting my son to sit still and learn is a huge deal! :)
text_fidelity_b: iTikes Map

text_fidelity_a:
Munchkin® Draw™ Bath Crayons Toddler Bath Toy, 5 Pack OK...so here's the deal with these...
5 stars for how much my 17mo old son LOVES them.
3 stars for how the crayon is constantly coming out of the plastic holder.
Averages to...4 stars.
No one is really addressing a few things, so I will...
these are super bright, amazing, soft crayons that are each a very distinct & different color.
In our particular tub, they color perfectly...but we have a somewhat "satin" finish as opposed to the shiny white finish which is what I imagine is the problem for people who say they don't work. I notice they color fantastically on dry or "damp" tub surfaces...but not as well on truly wet, slick surfaces.
We have a clear silicone table mat with a scene silkscreened on that I sometimes wet the back of and slap on the tub wall so he can color away on it like a coloring book page. Again, the crayons work perfectly when the surface is dry or damp, but can't get grippy enough for the color to stick when it's slick wet.

These crayons do constantly come out of the holders but I just keep pushing them back in. They also push back into the holder because the button is where my son grips the crayons in his tiny hands but when that happens he just moves on to another one, since there are 5.

I put these in to a bag of goodies I gave him for Valentine's Day and ours are still going strong with daily...prolific...color & scribble use on the tub, his tub toys, his picture mat, himself, and Mommy....head to toe. He does lots of "body art" with these, and he enjoys using his scrubby sponge for clean up and erasing his handywork, as much as he does the coloring part!

To me...these babies are worth their weight in gold if you have a budding artist on your hands, the right kind of tub surface, and teach the little virtuoso how to scrub it all clean to start with a fresh canvas! We LOVE...and I mean...LOVE them, and I can't see us ever being without them as my son is pretty much obsessed with all things artistic, and where he is allowed to just cut loose & get messy. These are perfect!

P.S. if you are concerned that teaching them to color on surfaces is a bad or confusing message, which makes perfect sense...I'd say that this is the way to let them be creative & have a blast but teach them that coloring on wall is only for the bathtub and only with these crayons....a concept they will need to learn.

I would recommend getting your first set somewhere that you can return them if they don't work on your tub. Also, get a matte finish silicone baking mat, or matte silicone placemat...wet the back, stick to wall & let them color on that. It works great for us!
text_fidelity_b: Munchkin® Draw™ Bath Crayons Toddler Bath Toy, 5 Pack

Fuairmee Foldable Canvas Toy Storage Basket,Creative Toy Storage Organizer with lids for Kids Room,Classroom,and Toy Storage and Outdoor Portable Container Storage Bins Good size for our legos. I was a little surprised by the material of the mat-- I thought the listing showed a three layered mat, but the one I received is only one layer, and it is a water resistant canvas type material. It's actually better this way, because often you need to be on a flat surface to have lego structures be able to stand independently. If the mat was too cushy it may make lego structures fall and be frustrating to work on top of, which would defy the whole point of having this easy cleanup basket! The mat attaches to the basket via velcro so you can use it together or separately (you don't need to have a basket attached to the mat while you're playing on it, for example). Makes cleanup so easy! I also like that you can throw the mat in the washing machine if that's the easiest way to clean up other things that may have gotten on there (like juice).

The basket itself is a canvas grey color, which fits in well with my couches (similar in color). The bright yellow mat, I feel draws kids to it, makes them excited to play, so it was a good choice overall.

First of all, the box is FULL of bricks., I dislike toys (or breakfast cereals!) that come in half-empty boxes. This is filled to the brim.

The treehouse set is not an easy set to build. Some parts of it are tricky, requiring gentle, patient hands.
Also, I have noticed in a few recent sets of things that I do not like. As I was building the bridge from one room to another, an essential piece was missing. It is LEGO, you can work around that sort of problem. In the last bag of the set, there was the missing piece. It was not needed on any of the steps for the last bag, it seems like it was "hidden" to frustrate me.

That said, when done it is simply beautiful. I built it with the fall leaves, and in spring, I will remove those and add the green leaves back!

Part of what makes this an advanced set is the physics of it. The small LEGO trunk should not be able to sustain the weight of the branches. However, some clever building techniques reinforce the trunk so it can easily carry the weight.

A spectacular build. Well worth the frustrations. A set to be enjoyed for many years to come!

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Here and Now World Edition Game This game is played a bit different than the regular Monopoly games. There are some similarities though. You get four tokens (and passports), so that seems to limit the number of people who can play. The object of the game is to collect passport stamps - the person to fill their passport first wins. The game starts off with all the major stamps placed on the board - a specific sized one for each property. There are some generic gray stamps that stay in the bank. Landing on a spot you have the option to buy that stamp or it can get auctioned off. When a player lands on a spot that you have the stamp for - the owner is paid a 'Visitor Fee' (basically like rent in the regular game). Another difference are the Here & Now cards and the Chance cards. I think these are what makes the game fun to play. The things the cards can let you do makes the game challenging - just when you think you're going to get ahead, another player can use one of their cards and put a damper on your play. Makes for some lively social interactions (if you get my drift). The dice is a bit different - one die has a icon in the place of the 1 pip (sort of reminds me of the speed die). That icon is the 'Sneaky Swap', it can also still be the 1 in some rolls.

Overall I have to say I've enjoyed trying out this new game (can't say the same for everybody here). I think we're still getting use to the way the game plays compared to regular Monopoly. The games tend to be a bit short - about an hour, but that might be because we still stop a bit and look at the rules to figure out what we're doing. Plus, given the different international locations on the board, we sometimes stop and an go look up where something is. (Helps to keep a globe handy). Fun game - and a bit educational.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Here and Now World Edition Game

This Little People Big Zoo is adorable in a big way. Set up time takes all of 2 minutes (the toughest part is freeing the toy from the packing securing it to the box).

The elephant by far is the best part--he is huge and there is so much about him to love and entertain. His parts move - and there is a little mouse on his back that when pressed you hears elephant sounds or music. You can feed him, pretend wash him, feed him, even weigh him on the huge scale. There's a teeter totter on top for the monkey or play kids to enjoy, a fence, some balls to come down the slide and all are perfectly sized for small hands but not too small.

Age states 1-5 but I think 5 year olds might be bored with this one. I do wish I could purchase another elephant as the little ones want to say with him at the same time.

For a toy under $40, this one is a definite pleaser.

text_fidelity_a:
JOY FOR ALL - Orange Tabby Cat - Interactive Companion Pets - Realistic & Lifelike My 75-year-old sister almost died from acute kidney failure following a major flare of autoimmune vasculitis. When I spoke with the doctors, they said she would not be able to keep her pets (two little dogs, two cats) because it would not be safe. She'll be on immunosuppressants from here on out, and exposure to live pets will be too dangerous.

I didn't realize there was such a thing as a robotic companion animal for adults, but a friend of ours said she was looking into a robotic dog from Japan. (Yeah, one of those really expensive futuristic plastic ones.)

I started researching and watching videos on YouTube, and I thought this Joy For All cat would be perfect for her. Her cats have always climbed up on the desk between her iMac monitor and her keyboard drawer and been a constant presence. Joy For All also has a dog version of this companion pet, but knowing my sister, it will be the cats she misses the most. This kitty can lie on her desk and be responsive to her when she needs it but go to sleep when she's embroiled in work.

I just got word my sister's new kitty has been delivered to her home and is waiting for her on the dining room table. She won't be out of rehab for at least a few weeks, but I'm so glad to know she won't be completely alone when she gets back home. I mean, hey, she refers to her Roomba as "My manservant, Raul" and talks to him, so I know she'll be really tickled with this robotic cat. I just thank goodness that these are available. I was really worried that my sister, who has had cats her whole life, was at risk of sinking into a bad depression after all she has been through. But what a great kitty this is! I want one, too!
text_fidelity_b: JOY FOR ALL - Orange Tabby Cat - Interactive Companion Pets - Realistic & Lifelike

text_fidelity_a: MONOPOLY: Fortnite Edition Board Game Inspired by Fortnite Video Game Ages 13 & Up This version of Monopoly does not use money! Genius idea for very little children! You gradually lose them all to the “bank” in the middle, but you can get more by passing Go or by landing on a plus-one space or by drawing a particular card. When you land on an available property, it’s yours for free. If you land on an owned property, you have to pay a green HP. Simple. This game is easy to understand, super fun, and quick for the short attention spans of young Fortnite players. Instead of everyone starting on Go, we all started on a homemade Battle Bus, jumping off and landing on whatever space you want. So we all started the game in different areas of the board and all started with a property. That helped the game go faster and was just plain fun to copy Fortnite. My kids have already played this 5 times in 2 days. Great buy! I rate this board game A+.

text_fidelity_a: Cephalofair Games: Gloomhaven, Award-Winning Strategy Board Game, For 1 to 4 Players, 60 to 120 Minute Play Time, For Ages 14 and up Me and my brothers have been buying board games for a while now. But no other board game takes as much dedication to play, store, and maintain, as this one. Aside from maybe pen and paper D&D. You get a box around the size of a family dog crammed with game. There's a reason there are YouTube videos dedicated to various ways to store this game's pieces. LMAO Along with various storage solutions sold on the internet. It's a beast to store. A beast to set up. But for all the work you put up with, is the actual game worth the hefty price tag? Hell yes. The ongoing campaign really gives you a sense of accomplishment as you trudge through one dungeon after another in your pursuit to fill your map with markers. Oh, and that map. We hung ours in a frame and laminated the countless stickers and markers so that they could be stuck to the frame glass with mounting strips. We proudly hang it on the wall showing everything we've done. Our band of mercenaries, Duke's Coinpurse, have opened up a LOT of content with hours and hours of gameplay. And we're not done with it by a long shot. Not even counting the expansion we bought for it. Now there are a few things that are kind of annoying. Like some of the personal quests that you may get that will want to complete content you already completed, or character classes you've already unlocked. Making your character's personal quest pointless or do some back tracking to complete. So there is kind of a miss-step in the order of reveals for some things. Your group is going to argue about rules in the rulebook. I can almost guarantee it. LOL Not that the rules are hard to understand, but there are so many that you're going to be dragging it out to double check something if you're anything like my group. LOL But it's about as close to an actual D&D campaign as you can get. The character classes you play aren't all that fleshed out aside from a backstory on the back of their card, and the game has city events and road events that play out with a scenario that the group chooses from a multiple choice outcome. But the immersion is a little lacking in that you don't actually "role play" per say as you do just dungeon crawl. But it's still a Hell of a lot of fun. Just prepare to work for that fun. Because it's a huge, long game. Scoundrel4Life
text_fidelity_b: Cephalofair Games: Gloomhaven, Award-Winning Strategy Board Game, For 1 to 4 Players, 60 to 120 Minute Play Time, For Ages 14 and up

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Color Shifters Playset (2-Pack) Mattel has combined 2 Hot Wheel Play Sets into one with this Sharkport Showdown Megapack. Five cars are included, making this set lots of fun. Putting the set together is easy with the enclosed directions. It's basically snapping plastic pieces together. There are a few stickers you put on first that give more detail and color to the set.

Once you get the set together, you will see that the set needs water. This means a water mess as the cars dive into the tanks to change colors. For inside play, I put down a cheap plastic tablecloth on the floor, with a towel nearby. This made indoor play a much more dry experience, keeping the water contained to the plastic cloth. But for the best experience, with no water to clean up- outdoors is best when weather permits it.

The Sharkport Set has 2 color change zones (cold and warm), along with a big mouth shark that chomps a car when the car hits the trigger. To release the car from the jaws of the shark, another car must come to the rescue, by hitting the shark. The boys ages 3 to about 7 find this set lots of fun. The other set- The Splash & Dash Set is simply a dunk tank for color changing the cars. It has a hidden trap door, so the car makes a splash.

You will find that having hot wheel tracks (NOT included) attached to this set, makes this set way more fun, as the boys love zooming around the tracks with the 5 included cars before getting eaten by the shark or getting the cars color changed. There are a couple tips I found, to make the experience better also. Don't over fill the water tanks. Also you will find the cold water gets warm quickly and the warm water cools down just as quick. This means you will have to constantly keep emptying and refilling the 3 water containers with warm and cold water, unless you do what I do.

I put some ice into the cold water tanks. The cold water stays good longer and the color changes instantly, as the ice does the trick. When the water is no longer icy cold, the colors do not change on the cars. As for the hot water, I also found out I can deal with that too, as I keep hot water in a thermos and let the kids add the water. NOT TOO HOT- just hot enough for children to handle. Between the thermos and ice- they are good to play for hours- and they do!

Sometimes the cars jam or get lint on the wheels, but these are minor fixes with a little push or cleaning the tire areas with a toothpick. Overall, if you use a thermos of warm water and ice in the cold water- they won't be running back and forth to the faucets making messes and will have lots of fun changing these 5 car's colors and of course they love those shark bites too. This is a fun, but messy set that the boys enjoy when you know how to set it up with your plastic cloth, ice and thermos.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Color Shifters Playset (2-Pack)

Educational Insights Design & Drill Bolt Buddies Recycling Truck Toy, Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+ The quality is great, and the concept is very creative. We play with this everyday, and think it’s fun, but there’s some thoughts I want to share:

-The clear bolts are somewhat difficult to find on the carpet. I wish the ends (tips) were colored to help make them stand out since they blend into the floor and surfaces.

-The drill bit is always falling out, and it’s also clear, so it can be hard to find it when it falls, and it’s cumbersome to have to keep putting it back in the drill repeatedly.

-The drill has two directions to tighten and loosen the bolts, which is adjusted with the sliding control. The drill itself works very well at tightening and loosening, but it gets a little involved helping my child make adjustments on the drill. My child wants to tighten and loosen a single bolt at a time before moving onto the next bolt, so we’re constantly flip-flopping the controls. Maybe slightly older preschoolers would be more independent using the drill, but I think a manual tool (like a screwdriver) would be the easiest to operate.

Our favorite part of this whole set is dropping all of the bolts in the back of the truck and then opening the hatch to watch all of them tumble out. My child thinks this is hilarious and is by far the best part!

In short, I think this whole set is a great concept, but is slightly overcomplicated. I really feel a simple screwdriver would help simplify the need to shift around buttons constantly, and would even help with dexterity and motor skills more than the cumbersome drill.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Design & Drill Bolt Buddies Recycling Truck Toy, Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
FurReal Friends Pax My Poopin Pup Plush Toy (Amazon Exclusive) I had high hopes for this little pooping doggo.. I purchased as a Christmas gift for my daughter (3 years old), who was obsessed with walking our dog and watching him pop (she’s a weirdo). Overall, she has gotten a fair amount of play and enjoyment out of the little fella, so I would *probably* purchase again.

Pros: He makes cute little doggy noises, he’s has soft fur.

Cons: He was much smaller than I expected (but my fault, as size is objective). He was overall much harder than I expected (other than his thin layer of fuzzy fur coat, he’s completely hard to the squeeze). He has wheels (which for some reason I thought he was more automatic than that). The leash is short (it was the perfect size for my tiny 3 year old when we bought it, but our 4 year old friend had to bend over to push it around). The treats / poo pellets are incredibly small. We lost a couple on christmas when we opened the gift.. and then a few more since. We have less than half left now (which I think is an accomplishment since we’ve had it almost a year!).

My toddler and her friends have enjoyed playing with it, but they have 1) been hurt by his hard material build (just minor boo boo, but still) 2) tried to eat the teeny pellet foods (cause, why not?) and 3) shoved other objects in its mouth that they weren’t supposed to. The design concept isn’t bad, but I do wish it was slightly bigger, with slightly bigger treats, a slightly longer leash, slightly more “squeezable”... you catch my drift. And with all that in mind, I probably would have gone with a different puppers.
text_fidelity_b: FurReal Friends Pax My Poopin Pup Plush Toy (Amazon Exclusive)

FELVOR Oceanic Dolphin Animal Shaped Puzzle with Box Stand - 8 x 11 Inches Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - Challenging Wooden Animal Puzzle 150 Pieces There made in China and being sold by Chinese company colorful puzzles on Amazon right now. I don’t know how/why, but this one shows to be sold by a US company. Nonetheless, it is still made in China and it is still the same sort of puzzle that you will find a lot of on Amazon.

This one has very nice packaging. Some of these puzzles come in very plain cardboard boxes. But this one comes in a very nice wooden box with a laser cut out of the design on top. So you can use it, of course, for the puzzle pieces… But you can also use it for things like pencils… Candies… Stamps… And so on. So it is certainly a multipurpose sort of wooden box. The wooden box measures just shy of 8” x 6” by one and three-quarter inches.

Though this puzzle has 150 pieces… Due to the fact that all of the pieces are very unique, and some of them are even of animals, this is not the easiest puzzle to put together. Which, I think is a nice thing. Some of the pieces are very small, so this is not the type of puzzle you will want to work around small children.

At the current price of twenty-five bucks this puzzle is a bit pricier than other options. If you look around, you will certainly find other puzzles for less… But… If what you really want is a dolphin puzzle, then this is a nice one.

Cheerson CX-10 Mini 29mm Diameter 4CH 2.4GHz 6 Axis Gyro RC Quadcopter UFO RTF Green I would recommend this drone as anyone's first drone, or as a cheap toy to keep in the office.

I've purchased several of these for the children in my family. The are small, light, and perfect for flying indoors. I've crashed mine several time from 8-10 feet up and they just fall about bounce off the ground. The basic-ness of this drone reinforces the skills needed to fly all drones at a very low entry cost. In this way you don't feel bad about trying things and crashing. The features are very basic with the only programmed/smart option is a flip. There is a sort of hidden option to unlock "acrobatic mode" (read the instructions to unlock) which is really just turning the sensitivity of the controller, but definitely a challenge for new flyers.

Once you master flying this little guy around jumping up to a bigger "smarter" drone is a piece of cake, and if anything goes wrong you have the fundamental skills to fly and land.

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Deluxe Wooden Magnetic Responsibility Chart With 90 Magnets This is an ok chart but with some issues. I really really wanted to love it because I've never been disappointed with Melissa & Doug products. For those wondering, it has the exact same tasks and pictures as the other Melissa & Doug Responsibility chart. It just does not have a spot for the child's name.

The good:
It's got a decent selection of tasks that. The visuals are great and easy to understand for my non-reader. The reward smileys are fun to pick out and have a rainbow selection of colors. It can easily hang (though it's a bit heavy).

The bad:
My board was warped, so the magnets don't fully stick. In addition, it was shipped with a plastic covering over the white boards. Unfortunately the magnets stuck to this plastic and peeled plastic off when trying to use it. This makes the magnets less sticky (see picture for example). This happened to more magnets than were good ones. There are only 26 choices of tasks, which make it pretty minimal. They are geared toward much younger kids, so my five year old won't use most of the magnets as he's already consistently doing these things. I wish there was a larger selection as the children age. There's not enough room for all of the extra magnets to be stored on the bottom half when not in use. One task does not fit if you have all of the smileys and all of the excess tasks down below.

Overall, I'm happy with the product but sure wish it didn't arrive with the above stated damage.

RoWood 3D Puzzles for Adults, Wooden Model Kits for Adults to Build, Birthday Gift for Adults & Teens (161 PCS)- Owl Clock In the beginning, this is quite easy to follow along with the directions. Most pieces fit well, it looks nice, and then...*crack*. I'm very careful when putting these kinds of things together, but I cracked a little tiny fitting, and there are no replacements. OK, fine, so that's one small fitting, won't affect much. Then, when crafting the pendulum, It says to place springs inside, along with a weight and nut, and when tightening the nut as instructed, the springs pushed the nut and fitting out the bottom of the pendulum. Another crack that I can't repair. Uh oh. Again, shouldn't effect too much of the function. Put the whole thing together, and...the hands of the clock are too tight on their fittings to turn properly. Towards the end of the manual, the instructions start failing a bit with the labeling, and I had to trust my instincts a bit to ensure that everything came together smoothly, and even wiht my mistakes, it looked very good.

I spent a little over two hours on this project, put it together entirely, although there is one missing fitting, clock hands that don't quite work, a coil that I really had to jam into place and a pendulum that isn't quite heavy enough.

Ultimately, this kit is an expert-level kit, but I should be an expert builder having made many of these before. While there is nothing obviously low-quality about the pieces, there are few that simply do not fit well, and a wide variety of fittings that are not well-labeled the farther you get into the manual.

text_fidelity_a: Nature Gift Store Kids Worm Farm Observation Kit Shipped with Live Worms I ordered this as a Christmas gift for my young daughter who is into all things worms, gardening, and composting. It estimated it would arrive December 5th, but it arrived a lot earlier. I think earlier shipping is always fine with the exception of live creatures. Being more than a month away, I was worried the worms wouldn't make it for the holidays. I contacted the seller right away to get tips on how to keep the worms alive and they were not helpful at all. I think I got a one or two sentence reply with no information. So I decided to do some research myself and I was able to keep them all alive without having to transfer them until the farm was opened on Christmas day. I kept them in the dark and a cool area of my house. I would take the cup out once a week to check on them. I'd water the soil a little every other week (just moist, not wet). I also set a couple carrot shavings, a torn up spinach leaf, and a broken egg shell on the top.  The worms did really well.  We transferred them as soon as she opened the farm.  The farm itself was disappointing in size and much smaller than I was expecting. It's more like the size of holding your two hands side by side. We plan to transfer them from the farm to her vermicompost bin in a few weeks.  She seems happy with the purchase, but overall I would not recommend this farm and would suggest creating your own with a little more research.
text_fidelity_b: Nature Gift Store Kids Worm Farm Observation Kit Shipped with Live Worms
